elena: quick heads-up — ran a 1k/2k/4k seq sweep on flashattn v3 integration branch (runtime/flashv3-kernel) and seeing a 12-18% regression p95 for >2k seq when KV cache is enabled :thinking_face:

miguel: ok can you paste the bench command and perf profile?

elena: command: `./scripts/bench_seq.sh --model llama-70b --seqs 100 --batch 8 --max-seq 4096 --kv-cache on --kernel flashv3`

elena: results (summary): `p50: 42ms, p95: 310ms` at 4k; baseline (flashv2) was `p50: 38ms, p95: 265ms`

ryan: does this repro on a single-GPU and multi-GPU config? could be kernel scheduling + cross-device memcpy for KV pages

elena: single-GPU (A100-80GB) only. nvprof shows more time in launch overhead and memory moves around attention kernel when cache hits are high

bench-bot: automated note — attached flamegraph: /ci/artifacts/1891234567/flashv3_flame.svg

arjun: is the kernel chooser falling back to a different kernel path because of sequence mod/stride? check the selector table in runtime/kernel_selector.cpp

miguel: I dug in — flashv3 kernel expects contiguous KV pointers for paged attention; our paged-KV allocator splits pages on growth so we get extra memcpy/pack steps. flashv2 had an optimized slow-path that avoided copies for certain strides.

elena: proposed quick fixes:
1) add a selector rule: if kv_allocated_pages > 1 and seq_len > 2048 -> prefer flashv2 kernel
2) add feature flag `ff_experimental_flashv3_kv_gating` default off for stable clusters
3) improve telemetry: emit `kernel_selected`, `kv_pages`, `copy_bytes`, `gpu_kernel_time_ms` per-request

ryan: +1 to the flag. for rollout we should do: dev -> staging (10%) -> prod-canaries (5%) -> prod (gradual). Also add automatic fallback: if p95 increases >10% for the canary pool, auto-disable ff for that pool.

arjun: adding telemetry is key. I suggest these metrics: `kernel` (v2/v3), `kv_pages`, `seq_len`, `batch_size`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `copy_bytes`, `gpu_util_pct`. will wire into console as a per-model heatmap

miguel: small perf note — batching heuristics interact badly with paged-KV. When batch contains mixed seq lengths, v3's kernel can't coalesce keys and we end up with smaller launches. We should modify the batcher to group by `kv_page_count` in addition to seq_len. A lightweight change: add `kv_bucket = min(kv_pages, 4)` and prefer same bucket when forming batch windows.

elena: code sketch for selector (pseudo):
```
if (feature_flag(ff_experimental_flashv3_kv_gating) == ON) {
  if (kv_pages > 1 && seq_len > 2048) kernel = FLASH_V2;
  else kernel = FLASH_V3;
} else {
  kernel = existing_kernel_picker(seq_len, hardware, model_arch);
}
```

ryan: CI checklist:
- [ ] fflag added and read from config service
- [ ] telemetry events emitted (low overhead)
- [ ] batcher updated to kv_bucket grouping (unit tests)
- [ ] canary pool with nodes labelled `flashv3-canary`
- [ ] rollback automation on p95/regressions

arjun: ops runbook snippet to add: how to flip ff across pools via console and CLI: `rictl feature set ff_experimental_flashv3_kv_gating --pool flashv3-canary --on`

miguel: one more observation — fused-attention microbench shows v3 is faster on contiguous KV and short seqs (<512), but paged-KV/mixed batches are the regression source. So flag + batch grouping is lowest-risk path.

elena: timeline proposal: today — land selector + flag + telemetry (dev), tomorrow — small staging canary with 10% traffic, next week — widen to prod canaries if stable. I'll open a PR with the selector and telemetry now.

ryan: please add a test that simulates high kv_pages and measures no-copies path to avoid regressions in future refactors

elena: noted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4723 (draft) :spiral_notepad:

arjun: tagging on docs: update docs/ops/flash-kernels.md with guidance about when to prefer v2 vs v3 and batcher knobs

elena: thanks all — i'll post back when canary numbers are in. :eyes:
